title: SSE: introduce fragment-rotation buffer and delimiter gating to prevent partial-JSON bleed-through
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Fixes an SSE edge case that could emit incomplete JSON objects when stream fragments overlap; improves tool/function-call ordering and compatibility with OpenAI-style clients; adds new unit and e2e streaming tests; no API changes.
description:
Summary: This PR introduces a lightweight fragment-rotation buffer and a delimiter gating policy in the SSE streamer to address a recurring class of production incidents where partial JSON blobs could be emitted to clients during reassembly windows. The bug manifested as truncated or interleaved JSON objects when: (1) upstream partial fragments arrived out-of-order or late, and (2) the streamer emitted a delimiter or tool-call sentinel immediately on flush.

Motivation: We saw two customer incidents where integrations using OpenAI-compatible clients failed to parse streaming responses during brief backpressure events (see SUP-4321). Prior fixes reduced most races but did not cover scenarios where a late fragment would rotate into an active slot after a delimiter was already emitted.

Approach:
- Introduce a circular fragment-rotation buffer (small, per-connection) that holds up to N in-flight fragments and rotates slots when late fragments arrive; rotation preserves original event ordering rather than clobbering the current tail.
- Add a delimiter gating policy: delimiters and tool/fn-call sentinels are deferred until the rotation buffer can be drained to a token boundary. This prevents emitting a boundary in the middle of a JSON token.
- Implement a lightweight seq-check on fragment headers: fragments now carry a 16-bit rotation epoch and a 32-bit offset; the streamer uses these to decide whether a fragment can be stitched or MUST be held for rotation.
- Rework parser state machine to expose a "boundary-safe" check used by gating. The change is non-invasive and falls back to the previous behavior when rotation buffering is disabled (config flag) for easier rollout.

Commits (high-level):
- Add rotation buffer data structures and unit tests (mchen/sse-rotbuf)
- Implement delimiter gating and boundary-safe API (mchen/sse-gate)
- Add OpenAI compatibility e2e harness with fuzz scenarios (mchen/e2e-compat-fuzz)
- Add metrics and tracing (sse.rotation.held, sse.delimiter.deferred, sse.rotate.evicted) (mchen/observability)
- Tests/fixes and CI adjustments after reviewer feedback (mchen/fixups)

Files changed (high level):
- sse/streamer/rotbuf.rs: new rotation buffer and invariants
- sse/streamer/gating.rs: gating policy and boundary-safe checks
- sse/streamer/parser.rs: state machine refactor to expose safe checks
- sse/protocol/fragments.proto: extended fragment header (epoch/offset)
- sse/tests/fuzz/compat_fuzz.go: new e2e fuzz harness using OpenAI client simulator
- sse/tests/unit/parser_tests.rs: additional token-boundary tests
- observability/metrics.yaml: new counters and dashboards
- docs/api/streaming.md: added compatibility notes and rollout toggle
- CHANGELOG.md: release note snippet

Tests and validation:
- Unit coverage added for rotation buffer edge cases (late arrival, eviction, wraparound) and boundary-safe checks.
- Fuzz e2e harness simulates partial deliveries, delayed fragments, interleaved tool-call sentinel injection, and real-world load patterns observed in incidents.
- Local compatibility run against openai-stream-sim shows previously failing cases now parse cleanly.

CI: All checks pass after two iterative fixes to the parser refactor. Notable CI jobs:
- unit: pass
- integration-streaming: pass (30/30 simulated scenarios)
- fuzz-e2e: pass (seeded reproducer cases validated)
- lint/format: pass

Performance: Microbenchmarks show ~0.9% median additional CPU per active stream under pathological rotation load (highly fragmented synthetic workload). Under typical production traffic the overhead is negligible because rotation buffering is rarely used. Observability/tracing added to measure rotation event rates so we can rollback if necessary.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag sse.enable_rotation_buffer (default off).
- Canary rollout to 10% of streaming traffic for 48 hours with alerting on sse.rotate.evicted > threshold and sse.delimiter.deferred spikes.
- Full rollout once canary is stable.

Review conversation (abridged):
- Diego Alvarez (review): "Nice design; my main concern is eviction semantics during high fragmentation. Can we ensure eviction never discards the last tool-call sentinel?"
- Maya: "Added an eviction invariant in rotbuf.rs and unit tests to protect sentinel boundaries; see commit mchen/sse-rotbuf."
- Priya Nair (review): "Parser refactor is much cleaner now. Please add a metric for deferred delimiters so we can alert."
- Maya: "Added sse.delimiter.deferred and a dashboard tile. Also added an integration test asserting deferred delimiters are bounded under normal load."
- Elena Petrova (approval): "Approach looks good, tests are exhaustive; approvable once CI green and canary knobs are exposed in config."
- Final thread: minor formatting nits addressed; Diego approved after review.

Merge outcome: merged to main via squash merge on 2026-03-03 by Maya Chen.

Notes on compatibility:
- This change is backward compatible at the wire protocol level; fragment header extension is optional (old agents are treated as epoch 0).
- OpenAI-compat shim updated to tolerate deferred delimiter timing and still synthesize proper function-call handoffs.

Known limitations and follow-ups:
- Current rotation buffer size default is small (4 slots); follow-up task ENG-10234 to experiment with adaptive sizing.
- We still see a corner case when multiple late fragments collide and exceed the buffer; a small number of these will log an eviction metric and fall back to the old behavior (emit delimiter). Those events are expected to be exceedingly rare and will be tracked via the new metrics.

Related work: superset of fixes from ENG-9876 and references to prior SSE fixes (see changelog).
notes: Merged via squash; migration-safe; rollout behind flag; follow-ups tracked in ENG-10234 and ENG-11000.
